title: The Five Righteous Men
notes: Based on a narration of Ibn Abbas in Sahih al-Bukhari: Wadd, Suwa, Yaghuth, Yauq and Nasr were the names of righteous men among the people of Nuh. When they died, their people grieved for them.
art: The five and the townspeople appear only as figures of light; their deeds here are imagined to show their goodness.
imagePrompt: Many generations later, a grand valley town at dusk with stone columns, porticos and terraces painted in warm Troy-style marble and bronze; five figures of steady white light seen at a distance, each in a different part of the town: one teaching seated children, one sharing a heavy load, one praying alone, one handing bread to another, one kneeling beside someone lying ill, the townspeople's lights brightening near them; then each of the five gently rising and fading, the town growing dimmer; finally the townspeople gathered in the square, lights low, heads bowed; warm marble and bronze cooling to grey dusk, parchment texture, no faces.

beats.say: Many generations later, there were righteous men among the people.
When they died, the people grieved for them.
